title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — AI Concepts and Terminology — Scope
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology

Scope: This document establishes terminology for AI and describes concepts in the field of AI. It can be used in the development of other standards and in support of communications among diverse interested parties or stakeholders. Applicable to all types of organizations.

Structure:
- Clause 3: Terms and definitions (7 subcategories, 117 terms)
- Clause 4: Abbreviated terms
- Clause 5: AI concepts
- Clause 6: AI system life cycle
- Clause 7: AI system functional overview
- Clause 8: AI ecosystem
- Clause 9: Fields of AI
- Clause 10: Applications of AI systems

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to AI
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.1: Terms related to AI

3.1.1 AI agent: automated entity that senses and responds to its environment and takes actions to achieve its goals.
3.1.2 AI component: functional element that constructs an AI system.
3.1.3 artificial intelligence (AI): <discipline> research and development of mechanisms and applications of AI systems.
3.1.4 artificial intelligence system (AI system): engineered system that generates outputs such as content, forecasts, recommendations or decisions for a given set of human-defined objectives.
3.1.5 autonomy / autonomous: characteristic of a system that is capable of modifying its intended domain of use or goal without external intervention, control or oversight.
3.1.6 application specific integrated circuit (ASIC): integrated circuit customized for a particular use.
3.1.7 automatic / automation / automated: pertaining to a process or system that, under specified conditions, functions without human intervention.
3.1.8 cognitive computing: category of AI systems that enables people and machines to interact more naturally.
3.1.9 continuous learning / continual learning / lifelong learning: incremental training of an AI system that takes place on an ongoing basis during the operation phase of the AI system life cycle.
3.1.10 connectionism / connectionist paradigm / connectionist model / connectionist approach: form of cognitive modelling that uses a network of interconnected units that generally are simple computational units.
3.1.11 data mining: computational process that extracts patterns by analysing quantitative data from different perspectives and dimensions, categorizing them, and summarizing potential relationships and impacts.
3.1.12 declarative knowledge: knowledge represented by facts, rules and theorems.
3.1.13 expert system: AI system that accumulates, combines and encapsulates knowledge provided by a human expert or experts in a specific domain to infer solutions to problems.
3.1.14 general AI (AGI / artificial general intelligence): type of AI system that addresses a broad range of tasks with a satisfactory level of performance.
3.1.15 genetic algorithm (GA): algorithm which simulates natural selection by creating and evolving a population of individuals (solutions) for optimization problems.
3.1.16 heteronomy / heteronomous: characteristic of a system operating under the constraint of external intervention, control or oversight.
3.1.17 inference: reasoning by which conclusions are derived from known premises.
3.1.18 internet of things (IoT): infrastructure of interconnected entities, people, systems and information resources together with services that process and react to information from the physical world and virtual world.
3.1.19 IoT device: entity of an IoT system that interacts and communicates with the physical world through sensing or actuating.
3.1.20 IoT system: system providing functionalities of IoT.
3.1.21 knowledge: <artificial intelligence> abstracted information about objects, events, concepts or rules, their relationships and properties, organized for goal-oriented systematic use.
3.1.22 life cycle: evolution of a system, product, service, project or other human-made entity, from conception through retirement.
3.1.23 model: physical, mathematical or otherwise logical representation of a system, entity, phenomenon, process or data.
3.1.24 narrow AI: type of AI system that is focused on defined tasks to address a specific problem.
3.1.25 performance: measurable result.
3.1.26 planning: <artificial intelligence> computational processes that compose a workflow out of a set of actions, aiming at reaching a specified goal.
3.1.27 prediction: primary output of an AI system when provided with input data or information.
3.1.28 procedural knowledge: knowledge which explicitly indicates the steps to be taken in order to solve a problem or to reach a goal.
3.1.29 robot: automation system with actuators that performs intended tasks in the physical world, by means of sensing its environment and a software control system.
3.1.30 robotics: science and practice of designing, manufacturing and applying robots.
3.1.31 semantic computing: field of computing that aims to identify the meanings of computational content and user intentions and to express them in a machine-processable form.
3.1.32 soft computing: field of computing that is tolerant of and exploits imprecision, uncertainty and partial truth to make problem-solving more tractable and robust.
3.1.33 symbolic AI: AI based on techniques and models that manipulate symbols and structures according to explicitly defined rules to obtain inferences.
3.1.34 subsymbolic AI: AI based on techniques and models that use an implicit encoding of information, that can be derived from experience or raw data.
3.1.35 task: <artificial intelligence> action required to achieve a specific goal.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to data
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.2: Terms related to data

3.2.1 data annotation: process of attaching a set of descriptive information to data without any change to that data.
3.2.2 data quality checking: process in which data is examined for completeness, bias and other factors which affect its usefulness for an AI system.
3.2.3 data augmentation: process of creating synthetic samples by modifying or utilizing the existing data.
3.2.4 data sampling: process to select a subset of data samples intended to present patterns and trends similar to that of the larger dataset being analysed.
3.2.5 dataset: collection of data with a shared format.
3.2.6 exploratory data analysis (EDA): initial examination of data to determine its salient characteristics and assess its quality.
3.2.7 ground truth: value of the target variable for a particular item of labelled input data.
3.2.8 imputation: procedure where missing data are replaced by estimated or modelled data.
3.2.9 input data: data for which an AI system calculates a predicted output or inference.
3.2.10 label: target variable assigned to a sample.
3.2.11 personally identifiable information (PII) / personal data: any information that can be used to establish a link between the information and the natural person to whom such information relates, or is or can be directly or indirectly linked to a natural person.
3.2.12 production data: data acquired during the operation phase of an AI system, for which a deployed AI system calculates a predicted output or inference.
3.2.13 sample: atomic data element processed in quantities by a machine learning algorithm or an AI system.
3.2.14 test data / evaluation data: data used to assess the performance of a final model.
3.2.15 validation data / development data: data used to compare the performance of different candidate models.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to machine learning
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.3: Terms related to machine learning

3.3.1 Bayesian network: probabilistic model that uses Bayesian inference for probability computations using a directed acyclic graph.
3.3.2 decision tree: model for which inference is encoded as paths from the root to a leaf node in a tree structure.
3.3.3 human-machine teaming: integration of human interaction with machine intelligence capabilities.
3.3.4 hyperparameter: characteristic of a machine learning algorithm that affects its learning process.
3.3.5 machine learning (ML): process of optimizing model parameters through computational techniques, such that the model's behaviour reflects the data or experience.
3.3.6 machine learning algorithm: algorithm to determine parameters of a machine learning model from data according to given criteria.
3.3.7 machine learning model: mathematical construct that generates an inference or prediction based on input data or information.
3.3.8 parameter / model parameter: internal variable of a model that affects how it computes its outputs.
3.3.9 reinforcement learning (RL): learning of an optimal sequence of actions to maximize a reward through interaction with an environment.
3.3.10 retraining: updating a trained model by training with different training data.
3.3.11 semi-supervised machine learning: machine learning that makes use of both labelled and unlabelled data during training.
3.3.12 supervised machine learning: machine learning that makes only use of labelled data during training.
3.3.13 support vector machine (SVM): machine learning algorithm that finds decision boundaries with maximal margins.
3.3.14 trained model: result of model training.
3.3.15 training / model training: process to determine or to improve the parameters of a machine learning model, based on a machine learning algorithm, by using training data.
3.3.16 training data: data used to train a machine learning model.
3.3.17 unsupervised machine learning: machine learning that makes only use of unlabelled data during training.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to neural networks
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.4: Terms related to neural networks

3.4.1 activation function: function applied to the weighted combination of all inputs to a neuron.
3.4.2 convolutional neural network (CNN / DCNN / deep convolutional neural network): feed forward neural network using convolution in at least one of its layers.
3.4.3 convolution: mathematical operation involving a sliding dot product or cross-correlation of the input data.
3.4.4 deep learning / deep neural network learning: <artificial intelligence> approach to creating rich hierarchical representations through the training of neural networks with many hidden layers.
3.4.5 exploding gradient: phenomenon of backpropagation training in a neural network where large error gradients accumulate and result in very large updates to the weights, making the model unstable.
3.4.6 feed forward neural network (FFNN): neural network where information is fed from the input layer to the output layer in one direction only.
3.4.7 long short-term memory (LSTM): type of recurrent neural network that processes sequential data with a satisfactory performance for both long and short span dependencies.
3.4.8 neural network (NN / neural net / artificial neural network): <artificial intelligence> network of one or more layers of neurons connected by weighted links with adjustable weights, which takes input data and produces an output.
3.4.9 neuron: <artificial intelligence> primitive processing element which takes one or more input values and produces an output value by combining the input values and applying an activation function on the result.
3.4.10 recurrent neural network (RNN): neural network in which outputs from both the previous layer and the previous processing step are fed into the current layer.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to trustworthiness
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.5: Terms related to trustworthiness

3.5.1 accountable: answerable for actions, decisions and performance.
3.5.2 accountability: state of being accountable.
3.5.3 availability: property of being accessible and usable on demand by an authorized entity.
3.5.4 bias: systematic difference in treatment of certain objects, people or groups in comparison to others.
3.5.5 control: purposeful action on or in a process to meet specified objectives.
3.5.6 controllability / controllable: property of an AI system that allows a human or another external agent to intervene in the system's functioning.
3.5.7 explainability: property of an AI system to express important factors influencing the AI system results in a way that humans can understand.
3.5.8 predictability: property of an AI system that enables reliable assumptions by stakeholders about the output.
3.5.9 reliability: property of consistent intended behaviour and results.
3.5.10 resilience: ability of a system to recover operational condition quickly following an incident.
3.5.11 risk: effect of uncertainty on objectives.
3.5.12 robustness: ability of a system to maintain its level of performance under any circumstances.
3.5.13 stakeholder: any individual, group, or organization that can affect, be affected by or perceive itself to be affected by a decision or activity.
3.5.14 transparency (organization): property of an organization that appropriate activities and decisions are communicated to relevant stakeholders in a comprehensive, accessible and understandable manner.
3.5.15 transparency (system): property of a system that appropriate information about the system is made available to relevant stakeholders.
3.5.16 trustworthiness: ability to meet stakeholder expectations in a verifiable way.
3.5.17 verification: confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.
3.5.18 validation: confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to natural language processing
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.6: Terms related to natural language processing

3.6.1 automatic summarization: task of shortening a portion of natural language content or text while retaining important semantic information.
3.6.2 dialogue management: task of choosing the appropriate next move in a dialogue based on user input, the dialogue history and other contextual knowledge, to meet a desired goal.
3.6.3 emotion recognition: task of computationally identifying and categorizing emotions expressed in a piece of text, speech, video or image or combination thereof.
3.6.4 information retrieval (IR): task of retrieving relevant documents or parts of documents from a dataset, typically based on keyword or natural language queries.
3.6.5 machine translation (MT): task of automated translation of text or speech from one natural language to another using a computer system.
3.6.6 named entity recognition (NER): task of recognizing and labelling the denotational names of entities and their categories for sequences of words in a stream of text or speech.
3.6.7 natural language: language that is or was in active use in a community of people and whose rules are deduced from usage.
3.6.8 natural language generation (NLG): task of converting data carrying semantics into natural language.
3.6.9 natural language processing (NLP) — system: information processing based upon natural language understanding or natural language generation.
3.6.10 natural language processing (NLP) — discipline: discipline concerned with the way systems acquire, process and interpret natural language.
3.6.11 natural language understanding (NLU / natural language comprehension): extraction of information, by a functional unit, from text or speech communicated to it in a natural language, and the production of a description for both the given text or speech and what it represents.
3.6.12 optical character recognition (OCR): conversion of images of typed, printed or handwritten text into machine-encoded text.
3.6.13 part-of-speech tagging: task of assigning a category (e.g. verb, noun, adjective) to a word based on its grammatical properties.
3.6.14 question answering: task of determining the most appropriate answer to a question provided in natural language.
3.6.15 relationship extraction / relation extraction: task of identifying relationships among entities mentioned in a text.
3.6.16 sentiment analysis: task of computationally identifying and categorizing opinions expressed in a piece of text, speech or image, to determine a range of feeling such as from positive to negative.
3.6.17 speech recognition / speech-to-text (STT): conversion, by a functional unit, of a speech signal to a representation of the content of the speech.
3.6.18 speech synthesis / text-to-speech (TTS): generation of artificial speech.

title: AI concepts and terminology — Terms related to computer vision
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 3.7: Terms related to computer vision

3.7.1 computer vision: capability of a functional unit to acquire, process and interpret data representing images or video.
3.7.2 face recognition: automatic pattern recognition comparing stored images of human faces with the image of an actual face, indicating any matching, if it exists, and any data, if they exist, identifying the person to whom the face belongs.
3.7.3 image: <digital> graphical content intended to be presented visually.
3.7.4 image recognition: image classification process that classifies object(s), pattern(s) or concept(s) in an image.

Abbreviated terms (Clause 4): API (application programming interface), CPS (cyber-physical systems), CPU (central processing unit), CRISP-DM (cross-industry process model for data mining), DNN (deep neural network), DSP (digital signal processor), FPGA (field-programmable gate array), GPU (graphics processing unit), HMM (hidden Markov model), IT (information technology), KDD (knowledge discovery in data), NPU (neural network processing unit), OECD (organisation for economic co-operation and development), POS (part of speech).

title: AI concepts and terminology — AI concepts overview
text:
ISO/IEC 22989:2022 — Clause 5: AI concepts

5.2 From strong and weak AI to general and narrow AI: General AI (AGI) addresses a broad range of tasks; narrow AI is focused on specific problems.
5.3 Agent: AI agents sense environments and take goal-directed actions.
5.4 Knowledge: AI knowledge is abstracted, organized information for goal-oriented use; does not imply cognitive understanding.
5.5 Cognition and cognitive computing: AI systems enabling natural human-machine interaction.
5.7 Soft computing: tolerant of imprecision, uncertainty, partial truth.
5.8 Genetic algorithms: simulate natural selection for optimization.
5.9 Symbolic vs subsymbolic AI: symbolic uses explicit rules; subsymbolic derives patterns from data statistically.
5.11 Machine learning concepts: supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, reinforcement learning, transfer learning, training/validation/test data split.
5.12 ML algorithms: neural networks, Bayesian networks, decision trees, support vector machines.
5.13 Autonomy, heteronomy and automation: spectrum from fully automated to fully human-controlled.
5.14 IoT and cyber-physical systems: AI embedded in connected physical devices.
5.15 Trustworthiness properties: robustness, reliability, availability, resilience, controllability, explainability, predictability, transparency, bias and fairness.
5.16 AI verification and validation.
5.17 Jurisdictional issues: regulatory and legal aspects of AI deployment.
5.18 Societal impact: broader effects of AI on society.
5.19 AI stakeholder roles: AI provider, producer, customer, partner, subject, relevant authorities.

Clause 6 — AI system life cycle stages: inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, continuous validation, re-evaluation, retirement.

Clause 7 — AI system functional overview: data and information, knowledge and learning, predictions and decisions, actions.

Clauses 9-10 — Fields and applications: computer vision, NLP, data mining, planning; fraud detection, autonomous vehicles, predictive maintenance.
